title: Fireworks Nexus: drop-in open frontier intelligence for teams with budgets
gist: An installer points existing coding harnesses at Fireworks-served open models. A trained difficulty scorer sends routine work to an open model and passes hard work through to the customer's own key at a frontier lab. It scores each turn and weighs cache hits.
changes: A second provider shipping the same split, open for routine and frontier for hard, from the open-model side. The provider owns the routing decision while the customer keeps the harness.
caveats: The router launched as a research preview and its evidence is thin: preliminary tests at two customers, and a typical 3 to 5x saving stated with no data. In Fireworks' own benchmark the open model matched the frontier one on score but used about ten times the tokens per task.

numbers.baseline: the customers' previous all-frontier setup, preliminary

bears_on.note: Open for routine work, frontier behind the customer's own key for hard work, in one harness.

retired_why: Its one number was the vendor's preliminary figure for two customers. An outside index has since measured the same router against the best model in its pool.
